passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and the notes thereto included in Item 8., "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data." Recent and Significant Events Olympus Energy Acquisition Our results of operation for 2025 reflect our acquisition (the Olympus Energy Acquisition) of certain oil and gas properties and related upstream and midstream assets from Olympus Energy LLC, Hyperion Midstream LLC and Bow & Arrow Land Company LLC (collectively, Olympus Energy), which was completed on July 1, 2025. See Note 11 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further discussion of the Olympus Energy Acquisition. Midstream Joint Venture Transaction Our results of operation for 2025 reflect the impact of the Midstream Joint Venture Transaction (defined in Note 9 to the Consolidated Financial Statements), where we received $3.5 billion of cash consideration from a third-party investor in exchange for a noncontrolling equity interest in the Midstream Joint Venture. The Midstream Joint Venture Transaction was completed on December 30, 2024. NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestitures and NEPA Gathering System Acquisition Beginning May 31, 2024, our results of operations reflect (i) our divestiture (the First NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestiture) of an undivided 40% interest in our non-operated natural gas assets in Northeast Pennsylvania and (ii) our 100% ownership of the NEPA Gathering System (defined in Note 11 to the Consolidated Financial Statements) following our acquisition of additional ownership interests therein in connection with the NEPA Gathering System Acquisition (defined in Note 11 to the Consolidated Financial Statements) and the First NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestiture. In addition, our results of operations for 2025 reflect our divestiture (the Second NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestiture, and together with the First NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestiture, the NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestitures) of the remaining undivided 60% interest in our non-operated natural gas assets in Northeast Pennsylvania, which was completed on December 31, 2024. See Note 12 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further discussion of the NEPA Non-Operated Asset Divestitures. Equitrans Midstream Merger Beginning July 22, 2024, our results of operations reflect our operation of the assets acquired in the Equitrans Midstream Merger (defined in Note 11 to the Consolidated Financial Statements). Following the Equitrans Midstream Merger, the gathering and transmission services previously provided to us by Equitrans Midstream are provided to our Upstream segment by our Gathering and Transmission segments as affiliate transactions. As a result, our Upstream segment's third-party gathering expense decreased and its affiliate transportation and processing expense increased, and our Gathering and Transmission segments' affiliate revenue increased. As the affiliate expense and revenue are eliminated in consolidation, the net impact is a reduction in our consolidated transportation and processing expense. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: In addition to the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the following risk factors make an investment in us speculative or risky and should be considered in evaluating our business and future prospects. Note that additional risks not presently known to us or that are currently considered immaterial may also have a negative impact on our business and operations. If any of the events or circumstances described below actually occur, our business, financial condition or results of operations could suffer and the trading price of EQT common stock or other securities could decline. Risks Associated with Natural Gas Upstream, Midstream and Processing Operations Drilling for, producing, gathering, transmitting, storing and processing natural gas are high-risk and costly activities with many uncertainties. Our future financial position, cash flows and results of operations depend on the success of our operating activities, which are subject to numerous risks beyond our control. Many factors may curtail, delay, suspend or cancel our scheduled drilling projects, the development schedule of wells which we do not operate but in which we have a working interest (referred to as non-operated wells), and our gathering, transmission, storage and processing operations, including the following: • delays imposed by or resulting from compliance with regulatory requirements, including limitations resulting from permitting, wastewater disposal, emission of GHGs, and limitations on hydraulic fracturing; • shortages of or delays in obtaining equipment, rigs, pipe, materials, qualified personnel, water (for hydraulic fracturing activities) or other natural resources needed for our operations; • supply chain disruptions or labor shortage impacts; • equipment failures, accidents or other unexpected operational events; • lack of available gathering and water facilities or delays in the construction of gathering and water facilities; • aging infrastructure and mechanical or structural problems; • failure of equipment, facilities or new technology; • damage to pipelines, wells and storage assets, facilities, equipment, environmental controls and surrounding properties, and pipeline blockages or other operational interruptions, caused or exacerbated by natural phenomena, weather conditions, acts of sabotage, vandalism and terrorism; • security risks, including cybersecurity incidents; • inadvertent damage from construction, vehicles, and farm and utility equipment; • lack of available capacity on interconnecting transportation pipelines; • adverse weather conditions, such as flooding, droughts, freeze-offs, fires, landslides, blizzards and ice storms; • issues related to compliance with environmental regulations; • environmental hazards, such as natural gas leaks, oil and diesel spills, pipeline and tank ruptures, encountering naturally occurring radioactive materials, and unauthorized discharges of brine, well stimulation and completion fluids, toxic gases or other pollutants into the surface and subsurface environment; credit_strengths.text: EQT's upstream and midstream integration, enlarged by the Olympus Energy Acquisition and the Equitrans Midstream Merger, lifted revenue and operating income sharply in the latest fiscal year, with operating margin far above the Energy sector median and among the highest in the peer group.

Operating cash flow covers capital spending comfortably, leaving free cash flow that represents a solid share of debt and exceeds the sector median, while interest coverage sits above the peer median, indicating ample capacity to absorb cyclical gas-price swings.

key_risks.text: The disclosed risk factors emphasize that drilling, gathering, transmission and processing are high-risk activities exposed to permitting and regulatory delays, equipment and supply-chain shortages, aging infrastructure, pipeline blockages, weather and cybersecurity incidents, any of which could curtail volumes and cash flow.

Debt remains substantial and rose after the Equitrans Midstream Merger, with net leverage above the sector median and only modest headroom to the next leverage threshold; a moderate EBITDA decline or further debt-funded acquisition activity would pressure the indicative financial risk profile.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage and free cash flow to debt both compare favorably with sector medians, and operating cash flow is well in excess of interest expense, so scheduled debt service appears comfortably covered even under weaker realized natural gas prices.

Liquidity is the main constraint: cash is small relative to debt and the current ratio is below one and below the sector median, so near-term maturities and working-capital swings depend on revolver access and continued free cash flow generation.

overall_credit_view.text: We view EQT as a solid investment-grade style credit: scale, integrated midstream earnings and strong margins support cash generation, while leverage above the sector median and thin cash balances temper the profile. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, not a rating.

Our forward view is that free cash flow will continue to fund modest dividends and bolt-on acquisitions, keeping leverage broadly stable; however, a large debt-funded deal or sustained weak gas prices could push leverage toward the next threshold and warrant a more cautious stance.

credit_strengths.text: EQT 的上游與中游整合，因 Olympus Energy 收購及 Equitrans Midstream 合併而擴大，於最近一個財政年度大幅提升收入及營業利潤，營業利潤率遠高於能源行業中位數，並在同行中名列前茅。
營運現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋資本開支，留下自由現金流佔債務的比例穩健，並超過行業中位數，而利息覆蓋率亦高於同行中位數，顯示有充裕能力吸收天然氣價格的週期性波動。

key_risks.text: 披露的風險因素強調，鑽探、集輸、輸送及加工屬高風險活動，面臨許可及監管延誤、設備及供應鏈短缺、基礎設施老化、管道堵塞、天氣及網絡安全事件，任何一項均可能削減產量及現金流。
債務仍然龐大，並在 Equitrans Midstream 合併後上升，淨槓桿高於行業中位數，且距離下一個槓桿門檻的緩衝有限；EBITDA 適度下降或進一步以債務融資的收購活動，將對指示性財務風險狀況構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率及自由現金流對債務比率均優於行業中位數，而營運現金流遠超利息支出，因此即使已實現天然氣價格轉弱，預定債務償付似乎仍能輕鬆覆蓋。
流動性為主要制約：現金相對於債務規模較小，且流動比率低於一及低於行業中位數，因此短期到期債務及營運資金波動依賴循環信貸額度及持續產生自由現金流。

overall_credit_view.text: 我們視 EQT 為穩健的投資級別信用：規模、整合的中游盈利及強勁利潤率支持現金產生，而槓桿高於行業中位數及現金結餘薄弱則削弱其狀況。指示性財務風險狀況為極低，並非評級。
我們的前瞻觀點是，自由現金流將繼續為適度股息及補強型收購提供資金，使槓桿大致保持穩定；然而，大規模以債務融資的交易或天然氣價格持續疲弱，可能推動槓桿逼近下一個門檻，並需要採取更審慎的立場。
